title: Noun phrases
subtitle: Countable and uncountable nouns, articles and quantifiers

blocks.text: Countable nouns have a singular and a plural form. **That painting** is amazing. **Those paintings** are dreadful.

items: do not change in their plural form, e.g. **the sheep is …, the sheep are …**.
with hyphens usually form the plural by pluralising the key word, e.g. **brothers-in-law, over-achievers**.
with organisations and groups of people (e.g. **group/team/etc**), it often makes no difference whether the verb is singular or plural. **The government is/are** not doing anything to help the arts.

when we want to refer to a group, we use certain phrases ending in **of**. These include: **a flock of birds/sheep, a herd of cows/elephants, a pack of cards/dogs, a bunch of flowers/grapes/keys, a set of encyclopaedias/keys**.

blocks.text: Singular uncountable nouns only have a singular form. They only take verbs in the singular. **Is the information** reliable?

items: With singular uncountable nouns, if we want to describe one particular item, we have to use a phrase ending in **of** before the noun.

Common phrases include: **a bar of chocolate/soap, a bit of help/advice, a blade of grass, a block of concrete, a breath of fresh air, a drop of water, a grain of salt/sand, a gust of wind, a loaf of bread, a lump of sugar, a piece of bread/information, a scrap of paper, a sheet of paper, a slice of bread/cheese, a speck of dust/dirt, a spot of ink**.

blocks.text: Plural uncountable nouns only have a plural form. They only take verbs in the plural. **The scissors aren't** on the table.

items: With plural uncountable nouns, we can sometimes use **a pair of**, usually when we see something as having two parts/legs/etc, e.g. **a pair of binoculars/trousers/scissors/etc**.

blocks.text: Some uncountable nouns end in **-s** but are singular, e.g. **diabetes, news, physics, politics**.
Many nouns are countable with one meaning and uncountable with another meaning. These include: **cake, chicken, chocolate, damage, glass, hair, paper, time, wood, work**.
blocks.note: The table is made of **wood**. (uncountable = the material) · It's a picture of **a wood**. (countable = a small forest)

items: Some nouns which are usually uncountable are used as countable nouns in certain expressions, e.g. **a knowledge of, a great help**.

rows.example: **a couple of (the), a number of (the), both (of) (the), each (of the), either (of the), every, neither (of the), the entire, the whole (of) (the), (a) few (of the), only a few (of the), half (of) (the), many (of the), several (of the)**
**an amount of, a great deal of, a little (of the), little (of the), much (of the), only a little (of the)**
**all (of) (the), a lot of / lots of (the), all (of) (the), any (of the), enough (of the), more (of the), most (of the), no, none (of the), plenty of (the), some (of the)**

blocks.text: **a few** = some; **few** = not many; **only a few** = not many. **little** + countable noun = small; **little** + uncountable noun = not much; **a little** + uncountable noun = some.

rows.use: talking about one thing, but not being specific
rows.example: I'd like to go to **a concert** tonight but there's nothing good on.

rows.use: mentioning something for the first time
rows.example: I've had **a great idea**!
**A poet** sees the world differently. (= Poets see … )

blocks.text: We use **a** before a consonant **sound**, and **an** before a vowel **sound**. It is the sound, not the spelling, that is important.

items: We use **a/an** to show what group someone or something belongs to, or to classify it/him/her. **Liz is a modernist.**

rows.example: Is that **the band** you were talking about?
**The guitar** is one of the oldest musical instruments. (= Guitars are … )

rows.use: plural countable and uncountable nouns · being specific
rows.example: **The scales** are balanced to symbolise equality.
Who did **the publicity** for the show?

rows.use: with some adjectives to mean groups of people
rows.example: Pop music has always appealed more to **the young** than **the old**.

blocks.text: We often use **the** with physical things that are unique (e.g. **the moon, the Queen**). We often use **the** with superlatives (e.g. **the best**) and cardinal numbers (e.g. **the first**).

items: We can use **the** to mean the well-known or the famous. **I bumped into Damien Hirst, the artist, in the supermarket.** (= the well-known artist)

theory.title: Zero article: no article at all

rows.use: with plural countable and uncountable nouns · talking generally
rows.example: Don't let your young child use **scissors** unsupervised.

rows.use: with singular uncountable nouns · talking generally
rows.example: An artist always needs **inspiration**.

blocks.text: We often use no article for concepts (i.e. not physical things), e.g. **society, space, nature**.

theory.title: Articles by category and with particular phrases

rows.example: indefinite: **in an hour, in a second** · definite: **in the 1840s, in the winter, in the afternoon** · zero: **in 2010, in winter, in December, on Tuesday, at night**

indefinite: **have a job, work as a teacher, I met a very nice American last night** · definite: **the King, the Principal, the President, the British** · zero: **Russians, become President, go to work, be at work, have work to do**

indefinite: **Is there a beach near here?** · definite: **the Himalayas, the Pacific Ocean, the Seine, the Earth, the Antarctic, the USA, the UK, the Scilly Isles** · zero: **Mount Everest, Berlin, America, Antarctica, Jupiter, Fleet Street, Lake Michigan, Mykonos**

indefinite: **Is there a bank near here?** · definite: **the bank, the post office, go to the hospital/prison/school (as a visitor)** · zero: **go to school/hospital/prison (as a student/patient/prisoner)**

indefinite: **Play us a song!, I've got a tennis ball** · definite: **play the guitar, the media, on the radio, go to the cinema, watch the TV** · zero: **play tennis, play guitar, listen to music, on television, watch TV**
indefinite: **Does Switzerland have an army?** · definite: **the BBC, the police, the emergency services, the United Nations** · zero: **NATO**
indefinite: **have a lesson, take an exam** · definite: **in the first year** · zero: **geography, be in class/year/form 5**
indefinite: **take a taxi, catch a bus/train** · definite: **in the car/taxi, on the bus/plane** · zero: **go by car/plane, go home, go by car/plane**
indefinite: **have a cold/headache/toothache/stomach ache** · definite: **have the flu/measles** · zero: **have flu/measles/toothache/stomach ache**
